items.title: Joe Williams interviewed by Leslie Gourse, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: Milt Hinton, Kenny Burrell, oh boy, Romeo Penque, Harold Lookofsky.

ctx.x: Harry “Sweets” Edison, and I like that Bohanon, the trombonist you worked with, and so many of them. I mean I love them. Jimmy Jones and everyone.
Yup, yup, yup, yup, yup. Hank Jones, Jimmy Jones, Osie Johnson, Milt Hinton, Kenny Burrell, oh boy, Romeo Penque, Harold Lookofsky. Really all these wonderful — Zoot Sims, Frank Foster, and —
And the Jones-Lewis band. The Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band.

items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Joe Williams was the vocalist [laugh]. He‟d get a good band [unintelligible] saxophone and I was doing fairly well on bass

ctx.x: Yeah. This Johnny Long is a trumpet player. Not a good trumpet player but a very wise guy. He had the club dates scene covered like Mitch Roberts. His name is Johnny Long and he wasn‟t a good trumpet player but he was wise enough to get good guys all the time. Joe Williams was the vocalist [laugh]. He‟d get a good band [unintelligible] saxophone and I was doing fairly well on bass, and we played Baker‟s Casino and all the Saturday night things and played the Warrick Hall, the $3 gigs and $9 gigs.
That was a lot of money in those days.
